title: Amount of the Return Balance Payment — Kestrel Advantage Balloon Return Charges
content:
The return balance payment on a returned Kestrel Advantage Balloon Retail Installment Sale Contract is built from the return charges and the fees that stood on the contract before the return.

## Definitions

- **Return charges.** The return charges are the excess mileage charge, the excess wear charge and the return fee billed on the contract for the return: the total of the return charge entries of those three kinds in the contract's posting history.
- **Fees standing from before the return.** The fees due balance less the return charges, never below zero.
- **Return balance payment.** The fees standing from before the return plus the return charges, paid in one payment and rounded to the cent.

## How the payment is put together

The part of the return charges paid now is the whole of the return charges; where more than one figure is set for the part of the return charges paid now, the larger is used. The collected part of the fees standing from before the return is added to it, every amount moved to later installments is then taken off and every amount added upfront is then added. The return balance payment never falls below zero, never exceeds the fees due balance and is rounded to the cent.

## Worked example (hypothetical figures)

| Item | USD |
|---|---|
| Excess mileage charge billed | 410.00 |
| Excess wear charge billed | 265.50 |
| Return fee billed | 300.00 |
| Return charges | 975.50 |
| Fees due balance | 1,020.50 |
| Fees standing from before the return | 45.00 |
| Return balance payment | 1,020.50 |

Had the fees due balance been 975.50, the fees standing from before the return would be zero and the payment 975.50.
